The tricky part is that grouping matters (two groups of four beats a group of five plus a group of three), so I'll solve it exactly with a small memoized search over the per-title count vector — provably optimal for any basket.

part.text:
Done. All 17 test cases in `book_store_test.go` pass, and the benchmark runs cleanly.

## What I implemented

`book_store.go` now computes the exact minimum price:

1. **`Cost(books []int) int`** counts copies per title (1–5) and hands off to the optimizer.
2. **`minCost`** is a memoized search over the per-title count vector: at each step it tries every possible next group — one copy of each title in any non-empty subset — paying the group's discounted price, and keeps the cheapest total. Since the state space is just the product of the copy counts (a few thousand states for the test baskets), it's fast and provably optimal for any basket.
3. **`groupPrice`** holds the per-group prices in cents: 800 / 1520 / 2160 / 2560 / 3000 for groups of 1–5 (the 0%/5%/10%/20%/25% discounts on $8 books).

The exact search handles the subtle cases a naive "largest group first" greedy would get wrong — e.g. two groups of four ($51.20) beating five-plus-three ($51.60), and the 22-book case where the optimum is four groups of four plus two groups of three.

No other files were touched.
